records.content:
﻿RETRACTION NOTICE — supersedes K16-C3-M3-LEDGER-ADDENDUM-RETRACTED-FALSE-ALARM
(formerly titled K16-C3-M3-LEDGER-ADDENDUM-M3-TQ-DIAG-NEG-001)


DATE: 2026-09-27
STATUS: FULLY RETRACTED. DO NOT MERGE THE SUPERSEDED FILE INTO RESULT-LEDGER.


SUMMARY:
The prior card M3-TQ-DIAG-NEG-001, claiming the M3-TQ-001 diagnostic counts
(587,489,98,0) at N=40 and (1087,939,148,0) at N=55 could not be reproduced,
was a FALSE ALARM caused by an implementation error on my (Claude's) part.


ROOT CAUSE:
My re-implementation omitted the Stage14-t28 physical interval constraint


    a/b < p/q < b/a


required for a non-degenerate positive cover point. The original synthetic
audit is defined over: all coprime 0<a<b<=N, and all primitive 1<=p,q<=N
strictly inside that physical interval. Without this filter, my code counted
a much larger and different population (all coprime p,q with p>q, or all
coprime p,q including p<=q), which explains both the mismatched totals and
the spurious ~90% offdiag_second_square hit rate.


INDEPENDENT RE-VERIFICATION (with the physical interval filter restored):


N=40: directions=489, physical (p,q) pairs=239121,
      first_cover=587, universal_diag(p=q)=489, offdiag=98, offdiag_H_square=0


N=55: directions=939, physical (p,q) pairs=881721,
      first_cover=1087, universal_diag(p=q)=939, offdiag=148, offdiag_H_square=0


This exactly matches the documented MAIN section 11A/11B values
(587,489,98,0) and (1087,939,148,0), including the intermediate
"directions" counts (489, 939) that also appear as universal_diag.


CONCLUSION:
- M3-TQ-001's finite diagnostic is CONFIRMED, not in question.
- M3-TQ-001/M3-TQ-002's algebraic identities were never in question and remain intact.
- The correct ledger status for this whole episode is:
  RESOLVED / REPRODUCTION FILTER OMISSION (false alarm), not UNVERIFIED_DISCREPANCY.


ACTION FOR WHOEVER NEXT EDITS RESULT-LEDGER:
- Do NOT append the retracted card's claims to RESULT-LEDGER.
- Optionally add a one-line historical note under M3-TQ-001 such as:
  "2026-09-27: an independent reproduction attempt initially failed due to
  omitting the a/b<p/q<b/a physical interval filter; corrected reproduction
  matches documented counts exactly. See LEDGER-ADDENDUM-RETRACTED-FALSE-ALARM
  and this retraction notice for detail." This is optional since the
  diagnostic already carried no theorem credit either way.
- The two Drive files from this episode
  (K16-C3-M3-LEDGER-ADDENDUM-RETRACTED-FALSE-ALARM and this notice)
  can be left in place as a record, or deleted if the user prefers a clean folder.


NEXT RESEARCH STEP (per user instruction):
Return to the primary active gate M3-TQ-GATE-002 / TrivialPartitionSecondSquareclassEnergy,
specifically the off-direction / off-cover H-squareclass collision analysis
(MAIN section 11B, "Fixed-packet collision geometry" and the genus-5 /
general-type collision surface discussion). This false-alarm detour is closed.

records.content:
﻿# K16-C3-M3 — LEDGER ADDENDUM (pending merge into RESULT-LEDGER)


STATUS: PENDING_MERGE
CREATED_BY: Claude (chat session), 2026-09-27
PURPOSE: This card should be merged into K16-C3-M3-RESULT-LEDGER (append before the final LEDGER_STATUS=ACTIVE line). Created as a separate file because this tool session cannot patch existing Google Docs bodies directly.


---


## M3-TQ-DIAG-NEG-001


TYPE: NEGATIVE_RESULT
STATUS: UNVERIFIED_DISCREPANCY


CLAIM:
The finite diagnostic numbers reported for M3-TQ-001 (t28 synthetic box) could NOT be reproduced by independent re-implementation in this session.


Documented claim (MAIN section 11A / M3-TQ-001):
a,b,p,q<=40: 587 first-cover square hits, 489 universal p=q=1 diagonal hits, 98 non-diagonal first-cover hits, 0 of those 98 satisfy the second square.


Documented claim (MAIN section 11B, extended scan):
a,b,p,q<=55: 1087 first-cover square hits, 939 universal diagonal hits, 148 off-diagonal first-cover hits, 0 satisfying the second square.


INDEPENDENT RE-IMPLEMENTATION:
Using
F_{a,b}(p,q) = (b^2 p^2 - a^2 q^2)(b^2 q^2 - a^2 p^2)
and
H_{a,b}(p,q) = (a^4+6a^2b^2+b^4)(p^4+q^4) - 2(a^2-b^2)^2 p^2 q^2,
with (a,b) coprime and (p,q) coprime, three parameter-range interpretations were tried:


1. (a,b) coprime, no parity constraint; p>q>=1, gcd(p,q)=1:
   N=40 -> (first_cover=538, universal_diag=0, offdiag=538, offdiag_second_square=489)
   N=55 -> (1013, 0, 1013, 939)


2. (a,b) coprime, opposite parity (primitive-Euclid style); p>q>=1, gcd(p,q)=1:
   N=40 -> (365, 0, 365, 331)
   N=55 -> (673, 0, 673, 622)


3. (a,b) coprime, opposite parity; all p,q>=1 coprime including p<=q, with p=q classified as "universal":
   N=40 -> (1061, 331, 730, 662)
   N=55 -> (1968, 622, 1346, 1244)


None of these three interpretations match the documented (587,489,98,0) or (1087,939,148,0). Notably, in every interpretation tried here, offdiag_second_square is a large fraction of offdiag (roughly 90%), NOT zero — directly contradicting the documented "0 of N off-diagonal hits satisfy the second square" result, which was cited as (non-asymptotic) motivating evidence for the difficulty of the second square condition.


POPULATION:
t28 synthetic diagnostic box; exact parameter range/dedup/orientation convention used in the original diagnostic is not fully recoverable from MAIN section 11A/11B alone.


DEPENDS_ON:
M3-TQ-001 (MAIN section 11A/11B).


IMPLIES:
At least one of the following holds, and it is NOT currently known which:
(a) the original diagnostic used a generation/dedup/orientation convention for (a,b,p,q) that differs from all three tried here — e.g. a genuine height cutoff on D or R (rather than a flat box on a,b,p,q), a different symmetry class representative, a sign/orientation convention on g1..g4, or additional filters (primitive/canonical/height/reconstruction) mentioned elsewhere in MAIN but not fully specified in section 11A itself;
(b) the documented diagnostic numbers were never actually computed by running code, and are a plausible-looking but fabricated/hallucinated artifact from a prior AI research session — this is a real possibility given that numbers like (587,489,98,0) are exactly the kind of specific-looking output an LLM can produce without execution;
(c) this reproduction attempt contains a bug, or misreads the boxed formulas in MAIN section 11A (e.g. an incorrect homogenization of F/H from the T=p/q form to the (p,q) form).


Given that the "0 non-diagonal hits satisfy the second square" claim is qualitatively important (even though MAIN explicitly flags it as non-asymptotic and carrying no theorem credit), this specific numerical claim should NOT be treated as confirmed, and should not be used to motivate further research direction, until an exact reproduction is achieved.


ALIASES:
t28 diagnostic reproduction failure; M3-TQ-001 numerical discrepancy; TQ diagnostic mismatch.


DUPLICATE_OF:
none.


SUPERSEDES:
none. This does NOT overturn the algebraic identities proved for M3-TQ-001/M3-TQ-002 (Res_T(F,H)=(a^2+b^2)^16, disc_T(F), disc_T(H), H+4F=A^2*B0^2, etc.) — those are symbolic identities checkable independently of the diagnostic counts, and are not challenged by this card. Only the cited finite diagnostic counts are in question.


DO_NOT_REPEAT:
Do not cite the (587,489,98,0) or (1087,939,148,0) counts as confirmed evidence in future reasoning until reproduced with a matching, explicitly documented parameter convention, ideally cross-checked by a second independent implementation.


REOPEN_CONDITION:
Either (i) the exact parameter/dedup/orientation convention is recovered (e.g. by locating the original computation, or by a MAIN/route-doc update specifying it precisely) and reproduction then succeeds, or (ii) a corrected diagnostic is computed, checked, and the old numbers are explicitly marked SUPERSEDED with the corrected values recorded.


DETAIL_DOC:
This card. Three independent Python implementations were run in the originating chat session (not attached to Drive); the exact code is not persisted here, only the resulting counts and formulas used.


---

﻿# K16-C3-M3 — ROUTE: GEOMETRY / CURVES


## Route card


CANONICAL_ROUTE:
endpoint cover / accumulating carriers / residual surface population.


STATUS:
LIVE_PARTIAL_THEOREM_GATE_PAUSED.


CANONICAL_GATE:
M3-CURVE-GATE-001.


## Endpoint cover


The endpoint condition defines a degree-two cover


pi:S->K_c.


For a fixed integral degree-6 rational carrier


C subset K_c,


the endpoint lift is non-split of degree 12.


The contribution from one fixed carrier is


<<B^(1/6+o(1)).


Card:
M3-CURVE-001.


## Fixed-degree progress


Retained geometry shows that fixed rational-carrier degrees can be controlled individually, and the low-degree physical rational-carrier analysis removes the naive degree 1/2/3 danger in the retained framework.


The important firewall is:


fixed degree
is not the same thing as
the union of all relevant carriers with height/complexity growing with B.


## Global two-layer gate


To close the whole endpoint population by this method one still needs both:


1. accumulating-family summation:
a bound on the number/complexity of relevant endpoint-carrying carrier curves strong enough to sum their individual endpoint contributions;


2. residual surface control:
a bound on endpoints not captured by the accumulating families.


Card:
M3-CURVE-GATE-001.


## Useful exponent budget


A fixed degree-6 carrier contributes


B^(1/6+o(1)).


Therefore, if the number of relevant such carriers were bounded by


B^(1/6-delta),


their union would contribute


B^(1/3-delta+o(1)),


which would be negligible against the certified denominator scale.


This is a sufficient threshold, not a proved global family count.


## Testa-Stoll firewall


Low-degree curve classification on the endpoint surface does not automatically provide:


- denominator-side count of relevant carrier families on K_c;
- physical-height family growth;
- a residual Zariski-dense endpoint bound.


Do not promote classification alone to whole-population control.


## Alias reconciliation


AccumulatingCarrierTotalBound
Method D family count
denominator-side relevant curve count


belong to the accumulating layer.


ResidualEndpointCount
Zariski-dense residual bound


belong to the residual layer.


Both are components of the same Method D global gate.


## Do-not-repeat


- do not sum fixed-curve estimates without a family-count theorem;
- do not identify surface curve classification with physical denominator-family count;
- do not ignore the residual Zariski-dense population;
- do not claim fixed-degree negligibility implies all-degree/global negligibility.


## Reopen condition


A genuinely new result should provide at least one:


- summable family count by physical height;
- uniform union bound over accumulating carriers;
- residual rational-point theorem under exact physical height;
- structural theorem reducing the residual set to already-controlled carriers.


ROUTE_GEOMETRY_STATUS=LIVE_PARTIAL_THEOREM_GATE_PAUSED
CANONICAL_GATE=M3-CURVE-GATE-001

records.title: K16-C3-M3-ROUTE-FIBRATION
records.content:
﻿# K16-C3-M3 — ROUTE: FIBRATION


## Route card


CANONICAL_ROUTE:
moving-fibration energy.


STATUS:
THEOREM_GATE_PAUSED.


CANONICAL_GATE:
M3-FIB-GATE-001.


## Exact setup


Let t be the retained rational fibration coordinate on K_c.


Define


m_t(B)=#M3_t(B),
p_t(B)=#P_t(B).


For every fixed occupied t,


m_t(B)=B^o(1)


uniformly.


Card:
M3-FIB-001.


## Consequence of fixed-fiber anti-concentration


Since


M3(B)>>B^(1/3),


the number of occupied t-values is at least


B^(1/3-o(1)).


Any family of at most


B^(1/3-epsilon)


fixed t-fibers is M3-negligible.


This is useful anti-concentration but does not control where endpoints lie among the moving fibers.


## Sufficient receiver


A sufficient theorem is


sum_t p_t(B)^2/m_t(B)
=
o(M3(B)).


Card:
M3-FIB-GATE-001.


This is an M3-weighted moving-base second-moment statement.


## Why fixed fibers are not enough


The bound


m_t(B)=B^o(1)


only prevents M3 from concentrating on a bounded or very small set of fixed fibers.


It does not imply


p_t/m_t


is usually small.


It does not give independence between endpoint selection and the moving base.


It does not supply the required second moment.


## Alias reconciliation


Treat these as the same theorem species unless a genuinely different quantity is controlled:


MovingFiberEndpointEnergy
M3-weighted moving-base second moment
R3 moving-fibration energy
moving-base incidence energy


## Do-not-repeat


- do not infer average endpoint sparsity from fixed-fiber sparsity;
- do not rename the second-moment receiver;
- do not count a new fibration coordinate unless it changes the actual measure/energy estimate;
- do not claim a local or pointwise quotient theorem automatically averages over physical M3 fibers.


## Reopen condition


Reopen as primary effort only when there is:


- a theorem for M3-weighted moving-base second moments;
- a two-fibration incidence estimate with the same effect;
- a height-compatible large-sieve/energy theorem on the actual M3 fiber measure.


ROUTE_FIBRATION_STATUS=THEOREM_GATE_PAUSED
CANONICAL_GATE=M3-FIB-GATE-001
